**What I found**

- **The main edge:** Polymarket's "Will X beat quarterly earnings?" markets don't settle on the usual adjusted earnings. They settle on whether **GAAP** (official accounting) earnings per share beat a fixed number set when the market opened. That number usually looks like the adjusted-earnings forecast, but GAAP often comes in well below adjusted because of one-off costs like legal provisions, restructuring, write-downs and investment losses. Traders are pricing these like ordinary "beats." I sent three research agents to check 14 companies, and most of them looked overpriced on YES.
